label: prop:habiro-tail-archimedean-action
title: Archimedean $\rho_\infty$ Habiro-tail action of $4_1$ is $\pi^2/5$ (golden-ratio dilogarithm), distinct from the geometric $\mathrm{Vol}$ face
html:
Archimedean specialisation. Conditional on the standard dilogarithm functional equations. Let S(q) = \sum_{n\ge 0} \prod_{j=1}^{n}(1-q^{j})(1-q^{-j}) be the 4_1 Kashaev–Habiro cyclotomic tail, evaluated at real q = e^{t} (the archimedean \rho_\infty face). Then:

  1. S is bar-even: S(q) = S(q^{-1}), since each factor (1-q^{j})(1-q^{-j}) is invariant under q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}.
  2. S is an alternating asymptotic series with (1-q^{j})(1-q^{-j}) = -4\sinh^{2}(jt/2); its optimal-truncation (minimal-term) resurgent action is 
      A_0 \;=\; -4\int_{0}^{\ln\varphi}\ln\!\bigl(2\sinh s\bigr)\,ds \;=\; \frac{\pi^{2}}{5},
    where \varphi = (1+\sqrt5)/2 is the golden ratio and the minimal term sits at \mathrm{arcsinh}(1/2) = \ln\varphi.

The evaluation reduces to the golden-ratio Landen dilogarithm value \mathrm{Li}_2(\varphi^{-2}) = \pi^{2}/15 - \ln^{2}\varphi, one of the classical closed-form values listed in [zagier-dilogarithm, §1]. It follows from Euler reflection, duplication, and Landen's identity at the golden points \psi+\psi^{2}=1, 1+\psi=\varphi, \psi/(1+\psi)=\psi^{2} (with \psi=\varphi^{-1}). Those three functional equations are recalled in [hakimoglu-brown2025, §1.1], whose own golden-ratio result is a different identity (\pi^2/100 as the real part of \mathrm{Li}_2 at a root of a quartic, §6).

Two faces of the same quantum object. The 4_1 quantum dilogarithm admits two distinct archimedean evaluations, which do not coincide:

Face Evaluation Trace field Resurgent action
Geometric / state-integral Faddeev \Phi_b at the substrate b (root-of-unity / Kashaev) \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\pi \approx 0.646
Archimedean \rho_\infty real-q Habiro tail S(q) \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5) \pi^{2}/5 \approx 1.974

The classical dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2 is the semiclassical (b\to 0) leading term of \Phi_b in both cases, but at different arguments — the geometric shape e^{i\pi/3} (giving \mathrm{Vol}, in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})) versus the golden ratio \varphi^{-2} (giving \pi^{2}/5, in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)). That the two faces carry different actions in different number fields is the \hbar \leftrightarrow 2\pi i/N resummation wall made exact: the state-integral and real-q Habiro evaluations are related by resummation, not by term-by-term reparametrisation.

Scope. This is a rigorous statement about the archimedean \rho_\infty (real-q) face. Because S is bar-even, the 4_1 Habiro tail carries no bar-odd datum, consistent with 4_1 amphichirality; the bar-odd (chiral) resurgence relevant to the Q_\beta odd channel must come from a chiral knot such as 5_2. Whether the real-q face — as opposed to the geometric state-integral face — is the physically relevant \rho_\infty evaluation for the Q_\beta observable is an open question; this proposition asserts only the mathematical identity, not a physical identification.

Relation to the proved resurgence results. The standard dictionary behind item 2 runs from a Habiro-ring element \Phi_K to the formal series F_K(x) = \Phi_K(e^{-1/x}) \in \mathbb{C}[[1/x]], its Borel transform G_K, and the median resummation S^{\mathrm{med}}_K; the Costin--Garoufalidis conjecture asks that G_K be resurgent, that S^{\mathrm{med}}_K be analytic on \mathrm{Re}\,x > 0 with radial limits at \tfrac{1}{2\pi i}\mathbb{Q}, and that those limits recover \Phi_K at roots of unity [crew2023, §1, eqs. (1.3)--(1.8) and Conj. 1.1]. Crew, Fantini, Goswami, Osburn and Wheeler prove the resurgence and median-resummation statements for Habiro elements that come from radial limits of partial theta series through a strange identity [crew2023, Thm. 1.2], and deduce the conjecture for the torus-knot families T(2,2u+1) and T(3,2^k) [crew2023, Cor. 1.5 and §3]. The hyperbolic knot 4_1 is not in that class, and the source supplies no strange identity for its tail, so the proved resurgence does not transfer to item 2: the action A_0 = \pi^2/5 above is an optimal-truncation statement about the real-q series and is not a consequence of [crew2023].

The state-integral face in the literature. The geometric face of the table is treated on the q-difference side by Garoufalidis and Wheeler, who work out the 4_1 equation tq\,f(qt;q) + (1-2t)\,f(t;q) + tq^{-1} f(q^{-1}t;q) = 0 completely: its solutions at t = 0 and t = \infty, their monodromy, residues and determinants, the associated state integral, the x-deformation, and an analytic lift of the colored Jones polynomial [garoufalidis-wheeler-modular, §1.5, Thm. 1.7, and \S§5.1--5.8]. That treatment concerns the state-integral face only; it makes no statement about the real-q tail S(q) of item 2.

Extension across the double-twist family. For the double-twist knots K(m,-p) (m,p \ge 1, with K(1,-1) = 4_1), the Lauridsen cyclotomic expansion and the q-hypergeometric Kontsevich--Zagier / strongly-unimodal root-of-unity dualities F_{m,p}(\zeta_N) = U_{m,p}(-1;\zeta_N^{-1}) and \mathcal{F}_{m,p}(\zeta_N) = \mathcal{U}_{m,p}(-1;\zeta_N^{-1}) of Lovejoy and Osburn [lovejoy-osburn, Thms. 1.1--1.2, Cors. 1.3--1.4, eq. (1.2)] write the real-q Habiro tail as \sum_{n\ge 0} C_{K(m,-p),n}(q)\prod_{j=1}^n (1-q^j)(1-q^{-j}). Under q \mapsto q^{-1} the Gaussian q-binomial chains swap m and p, giving C_{K(m,-p),n}(q^{-1}) = C_{K(p,-m),n}(q): bar-evenness therefore holds for the entire amphichiral diagonal K(m,-m) (including 8_3 = K(2,-2)), whereas off-diagonal knots such as 6_1 = K(1,-2) acquire a non-zero bar-odd part and asymmetric q > 1 versus q < 1 optimal-truncation actions. Unlike bar-evenness, the golden-ratio action \pi^2/5 is specific to the m = p = 1 base case where C_{K(1,-1),n}(q) = 1: on the q > 1 ray of K(2,-1) = 6_1^* (equivalently q < 1 of 6_1) the q^{n_1^2 + n_1} weight shifts the dilogarithm saddle to \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2}) at e^{u^*} = 1 + 1/\sqrt{2}, giving the exact octagonal action \pi^2/8, whereas the q > 1 ray of 6_1 (A_0^+ \approx 1.6433) and the amphichiral knot 8_3 = K(2,-2) (A_0 \approx 0.9913, distinct from \mathrm{Vol}(8_3)/\pi \approx 1.6648) are governed by a quartic inner saddle whose optimal-truncation actions are \mathbb{Q}-linearly independent of \pi^2 up to norm 10^4.
